classification.difficultyReason: Factorise a difference of squares, use parity to exhaust integer factor pairs, and include all independent sign combinations.

content.prompt: Find all the ordered pairs of integers such that $x^2-y^2=140$.

answer.short:
$(12,2),\ (12,-2),\ (-12,2),\ (-12,-2),\ (36,34),\ (36,-34),\ (-36,34),\ (-36,-34)$.

Factorise the difference of squares and consider the even factor pairs of $140$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-y^2&=140\\(x-y)(x+y)&=140\end{align*}$$
The integers $x-y$ and $x+y$ have the same parity. Their product is even, so both must be even. The positive even factor pairs of $140$ are $(2,70)$ and $(10,14)$.

For $x-y=2$ and $x+y=70$:
$$\begin{align*}2x&=72\\x&=36\\y&=70-36\\y&=34\end{align*}$$
For $x-y=10$ and $x+y=14$:
$$\begin{align*}2x&=24\\x&=12\\y&=14-12\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Swapping the factors changes the sign of $y$. Taking both factors negative gives the negative values of $x$. Equivalently, either sign of $x$ and either sign of $y$ leave their squares unchanged.

Thus all the ordered pairs are $(12,2)$, $(12,-2)$, $(-12,2)$, $(-12,-2)$, $(36,34)$, $(36,-34)$, $(-36,34)$ and $(-36,-34)$.
